source_text: Ἐνταῦθα δὴ μεγάλη τις οἰκονομία θεοῦ ἐγίνετο καὶ ἔλεος ἀμέτρητον ἀνεφαίνετο Ἰησοῦ, σπανίως μὲν ἐν τῇ ἀδελφότητι γεγονός, μὴ ἀπολειπόμενον δὲ τῆς τέχνης Χριστοῦ. Οἱ γὰρ κατὰ τὴν πρώτην σύλληψιν ἔξαρνοι γενόμενοι συνεχλείοντο καὶ αὐτοὶ καὶ μετεῖχον τῶν δεινῶν· οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ ὄφελός τι αὐτοῖς ἡ ἐξάρνησις ἐγίνετο, ἀλλ᾽ οἱ μὲν ὁμολογοῦντες ὃ καὶ ἦσαν, συνεκλείοντο ὡς Χριστιανοί, μηδεμιᾶς ἄλλης αἰτίας αὐτοῖς ἐπιφερομένης, οὗτοι δὲ λοιπὸν ὡς ἀνδροφόνοι καὶ μιαροὶ κατείχοντο, διττότερον παρὰ τοὺς λοιποὺς κολαζόμενοι. Ἐκείνους μὲν γὰρ ἐπεκούφιζεν ἡ χαρὰ τῆς μαρτυρίας καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων καὶ ἡ πρὸς τὸν Χριστὸν ἀγάπη καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πατρικόν, τούτους δὲ τὸ συνειδὸς μεγάλως ἐτιμωρεῖτο, ὥστε καὶ παρὰ τοῖς λοιποῖς ἅπασιν κατὰ τὰς παρόδους διαδήλους τὰς ὄψεις αὐτῶν εἶναι. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἱλαροὶ προῄεσαν, δόξης καὶ χάριτος πολλῆς ταῖς ὄψεσιν αὐτῶν συγκεκραμένης, ὥστε καὶ τὰ δεσμὰ κόσμον εὐπρεπῆ περικεῖσθαι αὐτοῖς, ὡς νύμφῃ κεκοσμημένῃ ἐν χρυσωτοῖς χρυσοῖς πεποικιλμένοις, τὴν εὐωδίαν ὀδωδότες ἅμα τὴν Χριστοῦ, ὥστε ἐνίους δόξαι καὶ μύρῳ κοσμικῷ κεχρῖσθαι αὐτούς· οἱ δὲ κατηφεῖς καὶ ταπεινοὶ καὶ δυσειδεῖς καὶ πάσης ἀσχημοσύνης ἀνάπλεοι, προσέτι δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ὀνειδιζόμενοι ὡς ἀγεννεῖς καὶ ἄνανδροι, ἀνδροφόνων μὲν ἐγκλήματα ἔχοντες, ἀπολωλεκότες δὲ τὴν πάντιμον καὶ ἔνδοξον καὶ ζωοποιὸν προσηγορίαν. Ταῦτα δὲ οἱ λοιποὶ θεωροῦντες ἐστηρίχθησαν, καὶ οἱ συλλαμβανόμενοι ἀδιστάκτως ὡμολόγουν, μηδὲ ἔννοιαν ἔχοντες διαβολικοῦ λογισμοῦ.
thought_title: Confessors strengthened and deniers shamed in prison
orientation: The writers describe what happened in prison after Bishop Pothinus was beaten and died, contrasting those who confess Christ with those who first denied the faith.
pass_a_gloss: Here indeed a great ordering of God came to be and immeasurable mercy of Jesus was shown, having happened rarely in the brothers and sisters in faith, but not falling short of the skill of Christ. For those who became those who denied the faith at the first arrest were shut up together also themselves and shared in the terrible things. For neither in this time did the denial become any benefit to them, but on the one hand those making profession of faith of what they also were were shut up together as Christians, with no other charge brought against them, and these on the other hand henceforth were held as murderers and polluted, being tortured double beyond the rest. For on the one hand the joy of being martyrs and the hope of the promised things and the love toward Christ and the fatherly spirit lightened those, and on the other hand conscience punished these greatly, so that even among all the rest their faces were plain to see in their goings past. For on the one hand they went forward cheerful, much glory and grace having been mixed together in their faces, so that even the bonds lay around them as seemly ornament, as on a bride adorned with embroidered golds inlaid with gold, breathing out at the same time the fragrance of Christ, so that some thought them even to have been anointed with perfume of the world. And on the other hand they were gloomy and low and unsightly to see and full of all unseemliness, and besides also reproached by the pagans as low born and unmanly, having on the one hand charges of murderers, but having lost the altogether honored and glorious and making alive appellation. And seeing these things the rest were made firm, and those being arrested confessed without wavering, having not even a thought of devilish reasoning.

pass_b_english: At this turn a great plan of God came to pass, and the immeasurable mercy of Jesus appeared. Such a thing has seldom happened among our brothers and sisters in faith, yet it fell in no way short of the art of Christ. Those who had denied the faith at the first arrest were shut in with the rest as well and shared in the hardships. Even now their denial did them no good at all. Those who were making profession of faith of what they truly were were shut in as Christians, with no other charge laid against them, while the others were at last held as murderers and as defiled, being tortured twice as severely as the rest.

Those who confessed were lightened by the joy of being martyrs and by hope in the promises and by love toward Christ and by the Spirit of the Father. Those who denied the faith were heavily punished by their own conscience, so that in their walk to trial their faces stood out plainly to everyone else. The one group went forward cheerful, with great glory and grace mingled on their faces, so that even their chains lay upon them like a fitting ornament, like a bride adorned in gold-embroidered robes richly varied with gold (Revelation 21:2), and they breathed out the fragrance of Christ (2 Corinthians 2:15), so that some supposed they had been anointed with earthly perfume.

The other group went forward gloomy and downcast and disfigured and full of every shameful mark, and they were reproached even by the pagans as ignoble and cowardly, charged as murderers and stripped of the all-honored and glorious and life-giving name. When the rest saw this, they were strengthened, and whenever any of our people were arrested they confessed without hesitation and gave no room even to a thought prompted by the devil.
